🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Alan Dysert, the actor best known as Sean Cudahy on the long-running ABC soap opera "All My Children," has died at 75.

Dysert died on Friday, October 23, 2026. His wife, Michele Dysert, announced his death on Sunday, October 25, in a message posted to his Facebook page, writing that her heart was broken and that she was grateful for "the love of a lifetime." She did not announce a cause of death, saying only that he had faced more than his share of health challenges over the years.

Born on June 12, 1951, and raised on a farm in Illinois, Dysert worked in real estate and did stand-up comedy before landing uncredited roles on the sitcom "Soap" in 1978 and in "Cheech & Chong's Next Movie" in 1980. He found his signature role as Sean Cudahy, the scheming con man and brother of Tom Cudahy on "All My Children," playing the character in the 1980s and returning for another stint from 1988 to 1990.

Beyond daytime television, Dysert worked as a producer, director, writer and musician. He wrote, directed, produced and acted in the 2015 film "The Senator," and appeared in films including "Two Weeks" and "The Grift." His final screen appearance came earlier this year in the Civil War drama "The Legend of Van Dorn," according to Entertainment Weekly.

He was also a beloved acting teacher. In 1991 he founded The Actor's School in the Nashville area, where he taught and mentored performers for decades. His wife described him as a "life changer" for his students.

In his 2023 memoir, "Lights, Camera, Cancer!," Dysert wrote about living with what he described as a rare, aggressive and incurable cancer, including four major cancer-related surgeries, a recurrence, chemotherapy and 29 CT scans. His wife said he wanted his family and friends to celebrate his life rather than mourn his passing.

He is survived by his wife, Michele, whom he married in 2008, and his sons, Cody and Cooper.

Sources: Announcement from Michele Dysert; USA Today; People; Entertainment Weekly; The Hollywood Reporter; Page Six.
